title: Smooth neighbourhood from a nonzero jet at one closed hypersurface point
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ smooth and locally of finite type, $M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, and $v\in\Gamma(X,M)$. Let $Z=Z(v)$ be its actual zero scheme [def-zl-prescribed-point-system-data] and $z\in Z$ a point whose image $x\in X$ is closed. If $\operatorname{prescribedPointJet}(M,x,v)\ne 0$, there is an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq Z$ of $z$ for which the composite $V\to Z\to X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. No parameter space, dimension bound, simultaneous jet map, or immersion of a complementary open occurs in this assertion.

source.place: Paragraph 2: nonzero first derivative and smoothness at the prescribed points

proof.text: Choose an affine open U containing x on which M has a free generator e, and put a equal to the coefficient of the section in this generator. Membership of x in the support of its actual zero scheme and basicOpen_coeff_eq imply that the germ of a belongs to the maximal ideal m. If this germ belonged to m squared, its product with the image of the germ of e under the stalk frame used in prescribedPointJet would also belong to m squared. The first factor of the prescribed jet would then be zero by Ideal.toCotangent_eq_zero. Thus the coefficient germ is not in m squared. This avoids comparing two frames by a unit.

Apply Scheme.Hom.finite_residueField_of_isClosed, the already proved locally finite-type form of the closed-point field theorem, directly at x. Algebraic closedness gives the inverse lift from kappa(x) to k. Compose it with the residue map to obtain a k-algebra map epsilon from the stalk R to k with kernel m. A k-linear functional on (ker epsilon)/(ker epsilon) squared detecting the nonzero class of a exists by vector-space dual separation. AlgHom.cotangentDerivation sends b to that functional evaluated at b minus its epsilon-residue; its Leibniz rule is already proved in the source library. Extend its values back to kappa(x). On each open, compose this point derivation with the germ map to obtain a derivation into the skyscraper module at x. It annihilates the base sections, since every base open containing p(x) is the whole spectrum of k. The universal property of relativeDifferentials gives a morphism to this skyscraper. Taking its stalk and evaluating gives an R-linear functional on the differential stalk; after tensoring with kappa(x), its value on da tensor 1 is the nonzero point derivative of a. Therefore relativeDifferentialValue holds.

Let s be unitHomEquiv applied to homOfGlobalSection M v. The inverse-equivalence identity identifies unitHomEquiv.symm s with that exact morphism, so the zero scheme is unchanged. Apply smooth_zeroLocus_of_relativeDifferentialValue to U, e, a, their coefficient equality and the nonzero differential. Its conclusion is precisely the required smooth open neighbourhood of z.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2; implemented using the local coefficient modulo m squared, point derivations, and the stalk-skyscraper adjunction (J1, 2026-10-26).

lean.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_neighborhood_of_prescribedPointJet
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [Smooth p] [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    (M : X.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (v : Γ(M, ⊤))
    (z : (homOfGlobalSection M v).zeroLocus.subscheme)
    (hclosed : IsClosed
      ({(homOfGlobalSection M v).zeroLocus.subschemeι z} : Set X))
    (hjet : prescribedPointJet M ((homOfGlobalSection M v).zeroLocus.subschemeι z) v ≠ 0) :
    ∃ V : (homOfGlobalSection M v).zeroLocus.subscheme.Opens,
      z ∈ V ∧ Smooth (V.ι ≫ (homOfGlobalSection M v).zeroLocus.subschemeι ≫ p)
